To modify, update the template and regenerate.
One edge of a run's chain. The producer names the step that writes a result and
the consumer the step that reads it, both by their position in the same run's
This is a relation and not a list on the step, because a step may read any
number of producers and a producer may feed any number of consumers. It is
what makes the chain a graph the engine can read: the questions "what is
waiting", "what may run now" and "what has to be rolled back, in what order"
are all queries over these rows and the steps' states, where they used to be a
parse of a document and a cursor.

One step of the chain a run was started with. workflow_step records a step
that ran and what came back; this records a step that *will* run, from the
moment the run starts, so the engine can answer what the chain is before it has
The chain is built per instance by the definition's build_steps, which is a
function of the start request and not of the definition alone — tenant
provisioning orders one step per kind its request names. A run therefore
carries its own chain rather than pointing at one, because the definition that
produced it may not produce the same chain twice and must never reshape a run

Records the execution of one step in a saga workflow, including the step
index, name, status, request/response payloads, and timing. Steps reference
their parent workflow instance via workflow_id.
